title: First Strike
description: Custom initiative tracker. A single slim bar of portraits across the top of the screen (or the classic vertical list), draggable anywhere and always on screen, so players see the turn order, who's who and who's up next without leaving their character sheet. Styled in the Embermark design language shared with Triad and Kronos (Cinzel/Spectral type, smoked-glass card, gold/ember/moss palette). A "Your turn" banner with a soft screen glow, an "up next" heads-up, and Delay / End turn buttons right in the bar for the active player, and the GM controls tucked into a small pill under it; an optional world setting hides hostile creatures' names and portraits from players. Picks up an encounter however it was started - First Strike's own Begin Encounter button, or Foundry's native right-click/combat-tracker toggle - and shows a Begin Encounter control inline until someone starts it. Always displays combatants sorted by current initiative, even if a roll made through Foundry's own native tracker hasn't re-sorted Foundry's internal turn order yet. Keeps the active turn pointed at the right combatant when a creature is added, removed, or has its initiative rolled/changed mid-fight, in any round. Auto-skip of defeated/hidden/delaying/surprised combatants respects direction, so stepping backward through a dead enemy lands on the previous living one instead of bouncing forward again. Players roll their own initiative locally (dialog and chat message on their own screen); only the final number is relayed to the GM's client to persist, since direct Combatant writes are rejected for players in this world. Marks the token itself as dead (native Foundry status) at 0 HP and clears it on healing. Delay/ready actions, an end-turn button so the active player can pass the turn themselves, upcoming-turn highlight, surprised-round-1 marking, roll-all-NPCs, keyboard shortcuts, and shared party HP visibility. Long combatant names truncate instead of pushing the initiative number off the row. No longer docks into Triad's tab (switching tabs meant losing the character sheet); Triad can still call the exposed roll API.
